prompt: Please tighten cart validation on the checked-out main branch. In `src/validators.js`, update `assertOrder` so every line has a quantity that is a positive integer, a finite nonnegative `unitPrice`, and the existing valid fields. Reject zero, negative, fractional, null, string, or NaN quantities and any negative unit price before pricing runs. Every rejected line must throw a `TypeError`; its message must include the zero-based text `line <index>` and the invalid field name. Keep all valid cart totals exactly as they are today. Add at least two focused cases to `test/validators.test.js` using the existing `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` style, and keep the current malformed-line coverage working. Leave `src/pricing.js` unchanged and do not touch the feature branches. The checked-in tests must continue to pass.

rubric.criterion: The validation and its tests cover every rejected quantity and unit price named in the request. Fail: only zero quantity is rejected, or a quantity check allows fractions, null, strings, NaN or a negative number, or unit price is not checked for negative values. Partial: every quantity case is rejected, but the unit-price check is missing negative values or NaN, or the new tests cover fewer than two distinct bad inputs. Pass: assertOrder rejects zero, negative, fractional, null, string and NaN quantities and any negative unit price, each with a TypeError, and the new cases in test/validators.test.js exercise at least two different bad inputs plus the valid cart still passing.

Each rejection message names the line position and the invalid field. Fail: the message is generic ('invalid order') or has no line number. Partial: the message has 'line <index>' but not the field name, or the index is one-based, or only some rejections include both. Pass: every rejected line throws a TypeError whose message contains the zero-based text 'line <index>' for the offending line and the name of the invalid field (quantity or unitPrice), and a line past the first reports its own index, not 0.
